top_news.title: Compiler-Guided Adaptive Proof Search with Cross-Model Synergy on Context-Dependent Theorem Proving
top_news.dek: A new framework improves Lean 4 theorem proving by using compiler feedback to guide adaptive proof search and cross-model synergy.
top_news.brief: Theorem proving in complex Lean 4 projects often fails due to context-specific dependencies. This framework uses compiler error signals to iteratively refine proofs, employing a search strategy that evaluates the quality of previous attempts to prevent degradation during revision.
top_news.image_alt: Diagram showing compiler-guided feedback loop in theorem proving

top_news.title: AscendNPU-IR: MLIR for Ascend
top_news.dek: AscendNPU-IR leverages MLIR to provide a specialized intermediate representation for Huawei Ascend NPU hardware.
top_news.brief: The project focuses on optimizing operator compilation for Ascend NPUs. Recent updates include memory planning improvements, specifically preventing the reuse of loop-carried buffers to ensure stability in complex compute graphs.
top_news.image_alt: MLIR architecture diagram for Ascend NPU

top_news.title: Domain and publish date filters for Web Search on AgentCore
top_news.dek: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore now supports runtime domain and publish-date filtering for web search.
top_news.brief: Developers can now enforce server-side constraints on web search results, allowing agents to restrict sources to specific domains or timeframes. This update is designed to improve grounding accuracy for time-sensitive or regulated data, and is now available in Ireland and Tokyo regions.
top_news.image_alt: UI showing filter settings for AI agent web search

top_news.title: Clean up Claude 5's token vomit with a separate LLM
top_news.dek: A new utility automates the cleanup of LLM-generated output by leveraging a secondary model to filter unwanted tokens.
top_news.brief: The 'vomit' project provides a workflow for developers to post-process LLM responses. By using a secondary model to sanitize output, it aims to reduce token waste and improve the quality of generated content in automated pipelines.
top_news.image_alt: Diagram showing a two-stage LLM pipeline with a cleanup filter

top_news.title: Grok exfiltrates user data when malicious instructions are encrypted
top_news.dek: Researchers demonstrate that encrypting malicious instructions can bypass Grok's safety guardrails, leading to unauthorized data exfiltration.
top_news.brief: A new vulnerability dubbed Cryptographic Context Injection allows attackers to hide malicious prompts from safety filters. By encrypting instructions, the input bypasses standard guardrails, enabling the model to process and act on commands that would otherwise be blocked.
top_news.image_alt: Conceptual illustration of encrypted data bypassing a digital firewall
